nodes.content: Recover relightable geometry and materials from three images under unknown illumination while quantifying ambiguity between shape, reflectance, and lighting.
requirements: Reduce held-out relighting LPIPS by 15% versus a matched point-estimate inverse renderer.
Achieve 85–95% coverage for nominal 90% predictive intervals on held-out relighting intensities.

nodes.content: Train a three-image-conditioned normalizing flow over shape, BRDF, and illumination latents; marginalize renderings into relighting predictions and intervals.
How can three-image inference preserve distinct geometry–BRDF–illumination explanations that produce similar observed pixels but different relightings?
Likelihood-trained flow with lighting augmentation retains competing shape–BRDF–light modes, achieving ≥15% lower LPIPS versus point estimates and 85–95% interval coverage.
On TriLight-Synth, compare augmented and unaugmented flows with matched point estimates using held-out relighting LPIPS and 90% intensity-interval coverage.
TriLight-Synth: augmented flow LPIPS 0.142 versus point-estimate 0.171 (17% lower); 90% intervals covered 91% versus unaugmented flow’s 76%.
Advance the lighting-augmented flow to real-image validation; TriLight-Synth meets both LPIPS reduction and predictive-coverage targets.
Validate the selected flow on DiLiGenT-MV using three images with withheld lighting labels; compare held-out LPIPS and 90% coverage.
Score held-out-light LPIPS versus a matched point renderer and flow 90% interval coverage on DiLiGenT-MV using three unknown-light inputs.
DiLiGenT-MV evaluation report containing held-out LPIPS comparisons, 90% interval coverage, and reproducible three-image input splits.
A four-component gauge-aware posterior mixture will preserve shape–BRDF–light alternatives, attaining 85–95% coverage without worsening augmented-flow LPIPS.
Train a four-component gauge-aware mixture on TriLight-Synth; compare held-out LPIPS, 90% coverage, and mode diversity against augmented flow.
TriLight-Synth mixture scored LPIPS 0.153 versus 0.142 for augmented flow, with 82% coverage for nominal 90% intervals.
Use a gauge-fixed diffusion posterior over geometry, BRDF, and illumination, with conformalized samples for calibrated relighting intervals.
Train gauge-fixed diffusion on TriLight-Synth; conformalize using separate calibration scenes, then test held-out LPIPS and coverage against matched point estimates.
Using r1’s DiLiGenT-MV splits, compare augmented flow and conformalized gauge-fixed diffusion on held-out-light LPIPS and 90% coverage.
DiLiGenT-MV: point/flow/diffusion LPIPS 0.200/0.181/0.166; flow/diffusion 90%-interval coverage 78%/91%, respectively.
Does diffusion’s 91% aggregate coverage conceal undercoverage on specular pixels under grazing held-out lights?
Despite 91% aggregate coverage, diffusion’s nominal 90% intervals cover under 85% of top-decile highlights at >70° incidence.
Measure diffusion’s 90% interval coverage on DiLiGenT-MV top-decile highlights under held-out lights at >70° incidence, with scene-bootstrap intervals.
DiLiGenT-MV top-decile highlights at >70° incidence showed 79% coverage (95% scene-bootstrap CI: 75–83%) versus 91% aggregate.
Audit diffusion’s 90% interval coverage on TriLight-Synth top-decile highlights at >70° incidence, stratified by BRDF roughness.
TriLight-Synth audit found swapped incidence bins in the shared evaluator; reanalyzed DiLiGenT-MV grazing highlights covered 89%, not 79%.
With corrected incidence bins, diffusion’s 90% intervals cover 85–95% of DiLiGenT-MV grazing highlights across BRDF roughness strata.
Reanalyze the original DiLiGenT-MV grazing-highlight samples using corrected incidence bins; bootstrap 90% interval coverage across BRDF roughness strata.
Corrected DiLiGenT-MV grazing highlights had 89% coverage (95% scene-bootstrap CI: 86–92%); smooth and rough BRDF strata reached 87% and 91%.
Retain diffusion with mandatory incidence-bin and roughness-stratified audits: apparent 79% coverage prompted investigation; corrected strata reach 87–91%.
Replicate diffusion on unseen three-image scenes, requiring ≥15% lower LPIPS versus matched point estimates and 85–95% corrected-bin coverage.
Derive object-disjoint DiLiGenT-MV partitions from r1’s splits; compare diffusion/point LPIPS and audit diffusion’s corrected-bin 90% coverage.
Revised DiLiGenT-MV report replaces r1’s splits with object-disjoint partitions and corrected incidence bins; diffusion LPIPS 0.178 versus 0.214, coverage 90%.
Distill gauge-fixed diffusion into diverse posterior particles, then apply roughness-conditioned conformal calibration for efficient three-image relighting.
Distill diffusion into 16 posterior particles; calibrate by roughness, then evaluate object-disjoint DiLiGenT-MV LPIPS, coverage, and inference time.
On r2’s object-disjoint splits, benchmark roughness-calibrated 16-particle distillation against diffusion and point baselines for LPIPS, corrected-bin coverage, and runtime.
Object-disjoint DiLiGenT-MV: particles achieved LPIPS 0.180 versus point estimate 0.214, 89% corrected-bin coverage, and 0.5 versus diffusion’s 6.2 seconds.
Rao–Blackwellize diffuse spherical-harmonic lighting over geometry–BRDF particles, sample specular illumination, and conformalize relighting intervals.
Can analytic diffuse-light marginalization reduce 16-particle Monte Carlo noise while preserving specular-light alternatives and 90% interval coverage?
Analytic diffuse-light marginalization cuts 16-particle predictive-mean variance ≥25% while retaining ≥89% coverage and LPIPS ≤0.180.
On object-disjoint DiLiGenT-MV, compare 20-seed predictive-mean variance, LPIPS, and corrected-bin coverage for Rao–Blackwellized versus standard 16-particle inference.
DiLiGenT-MV: Rao–Blackwellization cut predictive-mean variance 35% and yielded LPIPS 0.179, but corrected-bin coverage fell to 84%.
On DiLiGenT-MV, stratify Rao–Blackwellized versus standard particles by specular highlights; compare illumination-mode diversity, predictive-mean variance, LPIPS, and coverage.
On independent DiLiGenT-MV object folds, unmodified Rao–Blackwellization reduced variance 30%, reached LPIPS 0.179 and 90% aggregate coverage, retaining specular modes.
Analytic marginalization cuts variance ≥25% while preserving specular modes; highlight-conditioned calibration is needed for ≥89% corrected-bin coverage across object folds.
Fit highlight-conditioned calibration on separate scenes; reassess both DiLiGenT-MV folds for ≥25% variance reduction, specular modes, and ≥89% coverage.
Across both DiLiGenT-MV folds, highlight calibration restored corrected-bin coverage to 90–91%; variance fell 30–35%, with specular modes retained.
Adopt Rao–Blackwellized particles with highlight-conditioned calibration: initial 84% undercoverage resolved to 90–91% across folds; variance fell 30–35%.
On unseen LightStage-Objects, test adopted particles using three unknown-light inputs: ≥15% LPIPS reduction versus point estimates; 85–95% corrected-bin coverage.
Using r2’s corrected-bin protocol, evaluate adopted particles on three-input LightStage-Objects: LPIPS versus point estimates and 90% interval coverage.
Updated relighting report extends r2 to LightStage-Objects: particle LPIPS 0.199 versus point-estimate 0.240 (17% lower), corrected-bin coverage 89%.
Add conditional Shapley variance attribution to Rao–Blackwellized particles, separating geometry, BRDF, and lighting contributions to relighting uncertainty.
Compute conditional Shapley attributions on LightStage-Objects particles; validate with conditional latent swaps and recheck LPIPS and corrected-bin coverage.
Using r3’s LightStage-Objects particles, compare conditional Shapley rankings with latent-swap variance changes; reproduce LPIPS and corrected-bin coverage.
LightStage-Objects Shapley and conditional-swap rankings correlated at Spearman ρ=0.82; LPIPS remained 0.199 and corrected-bin coverage 89%.
Does aggregate ρ=0.82 mask unstable geometry-versus-BRDF Shapley rankings on glossy LightStage-Objects?
On glossy objects (roughness <0.2), geometry–BRDF Shapley rankings disagree with conditional-swap rankings in ≥30% of scenes.
On r3’s glossy LightStage-Objects (roughness <0.2), measure scene-level geometry–BRDF Shapley versus conditional-swap ranking disagreement.
Across 20 glossy LightStage-Objects scenes, geometry–BRDF Shapley and conditional-swap rankings disagreed in 8 (40%).
At least six of eight glossy-scene ranking conflicts have geometry–BRDF Shapley differences below 5% of predictive variance.
Using r3’s particles and e11’s attributions, count e12’s eight conflicts with geometry–BRDF Shapley gaps below 5% of predictive variance.
Only 3 of 8 glossy-scene conflicts had geometry–BRDF Shapley gaps below 5% of predictive variance.
Retain Shapley for aggregate attribution, but flag glossy geometry–BRDF rankings and report swap checks: 40% conflict, mostly substantive.
On unseen glossy scenes, audit geometry–BRDF Shapley rankings against swaps, flag conflicts, and verify ≥15% LPIPS reduction and 85–95% coverage.
Using r3’s particles and e12’s 40% baseline, audit unseen glossy scenes for ranking conflicts, LPIPS, and corrected-bin coverage.
Revised r3 adds unseen glossy-scene results: LPIPS 0.205 versus 0.246, corrected-bin coverage 90%, and seven of 20 attribution conflicts flagged.
Recompute r3 and r4 glossy-scene ranking conflicts, LPIPS, and corrected-bin coverage, checking ≥30% disagreement against latent swaps.
Audit reproduced 8/20 and 7/20 glossy ranking conflicts on r3/r4; r4 LPIPS 0.205 versus 0.246, coverage 90%.
Release relighting predictions with glossy attribution warnings: both audits show ≥35% ranking conflicts, yet LPIPS and coverage meet targets.
